coverage.description: Curated, source-cited examples; not an exhaustive history of NBA games or corrections.
coverage.statisticsPolicy: Only describe this observed sample. Do not infer a league-wide rate, rarity, average correction duration, or historical completeness.

originalReported.status: pre-correction official final, retrospectively stated by NBA.com

finalOfficial.status: corrected NBA final; corroborated by current ESPN box score

correctionAnnouncedAt.basis: The X status ID resolves to 02:44 UTC; NBA.com's embed displays 2:44 AM on Oct. 25 without seconds. Value is rounded to the minute.

originalProviderLine.qualification: CBS's captured provider display showed 10 points and 0/2 FT; this is a secondary-source observation, not a preserved NBA pre-correction box score.

correctedLine.qualification: NBC reports the corrected line includes all 11 points; ESPN's current box score shows 11 points and 1/2 FT.

playContext.event: De'Anthony Melton made the first of two free throws; the original game record credited him with two misses.

scoreImmediatelyAfter.derivation: NBC reports 91–67 at the attempt and a successful one-point free throw; NBA Rule 5 assigns one point to a successful free throw. No independently captured live-feed row for 92–67 is cited.

cause.summary: The NBA said game statisticians recorded both free throws as missed even though Melton made the first; the league then changed the official final by one point.
cause.individualOrProcessCause: The source describes the incorrect entry but does not establish why it happened; no motive or broader process failure is inferred.

timeline.event: Warriors win was initially recorded as 139–104; the NBA later identified the omitted made free throw.
NBA Official announced that the final was changed to 140–104.

timeline.at: 2024-10-25 (report updated 07:46; timezone not supplied on page)
timeline.event: NBA.com-hosted AP report explains the missed entry and the 139–104 to 140–104 correction.

evidence.claim: The NBA found an error and changed the final score from 139–104 to 140–104 after Golden State was not credited for a made third-quarter free throw.
The NBA.com-hosted report says game statisticians recorded Melton as missing both free throws although he made the first.
NBC Sports Bay Area reports the score was 91–67 at the attempt and says Melton's corrected line includes all 11 points.
ESPN's current box score shows 140–104 and Melton with 11 points and 1/2 FT.
CBS's captured gametracker scoreboard still displayed 139–104 and Melton with 10 points/0-for-2 FT, while its embedded AP story text said 140–104.

sourceDisagreements.observedAtPrecision: research fetch date only; exact acquisition time was not retained
sourceDisagreements.description: ESPN's current score table shows 140–104 while embedded AP recap text says 139–104. CBS's gametracker likewise showed 139–104 while its embedded AP copy said 140–104. These are conflicting fields within secondary-source pages, not additional NBA corrections.

limitations: The NBA-hosted historical game page rendered unrelated current schedule content during research; no historical NBA box-score snapshot was recovered.
The original Melton line is retained as a CBS provider observation, not as an independently archived NBA stat feed.
The one-point score after the free throw is arithmetic-derived and labelled as such.

cause.summary: The NBA's announcement identifies the first free throw as incorrectly entered as a miss and says the statistics were corrected. The Athletic reports that NBA League Operations SVP Tim Frank attributed it to human error and an in-arena statistician; the Athletic page returned HTTP 403 in this research pass, so that attribution is not treated as a directly inspected primary record.
cause.individualOrProcessCause: Reported by The Athletic, not stated in the accessible NBA Official X post; retain the attribution as secondary reporting rather than an independently verified causal finding.

timeline.event: Cleveland's initially reported final was 148–114; ESPN's embedded AP recap retains this value.
NBA Official announced the scoring correction; the final became 148–115.
ESPN's current table shows 148–115 while its embedded AP prose still states 148–114.

evidence.claim: NBA Official's post announces a score correction for Cavaliers–Wizards; The Athletic and AP-sourced reporting identify the change from 148–114 to 148–115.
The league's statement says Tre Johnson's first free throw at 8:15 of Q2 was incorrectly entered as missed; the accessible reporting says it was made.
The Athletic reports the pre-attempt score as Cleveland 50, Washington 39; 50–40 immediately after the make is a derived value, not a preserved live-feed observation.
ESPN's current recap score table and box score show 148–115, while the recap's embedded AP prose says 148–114.
The Athletic reports the corrected Tre Johnson line as 19 points and 2-of-3 free throws; this is secondary reporting, not a recovered historical NBA box score.

limitations: The Athletic article returned HTTP 403 to the research fetcher; its indexed text was visible and is linked for independent checking. The accessible AP-sourced Hoops Wire report corroborates the correction.
